summary: @onereach/expression-components 9.1.2 executes obfuscated Bun-only payload from preinstall hook
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime (pinned v1.3.13) from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases, extracts the platform-specific binary to a tmpdir, chmods it executable, and invokes it against the sibling file math_init.js via execFileSync. math_init.js is a 727,680-byte Bun-compiled bundle (`// @bun @bun-cjs`) using string-array rotation obfuscation (hex-scrambled identifiers, a shifted constants table, and a decoder function). The filename is a cover story: the package is advertised as a Vue expression-components library, has no documented need for Bun, and the obfuscated bundle bears no relation to Vue components. The alternate-runtime dropper pattern (fetching Bun specifically to execute a bundle that Node-based review does not naturally analyze) at npm install time places attacker-controlled obfuscated code on the installer's machine on every `npm install`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
